independent.summary: copyEntry snapshots autoScroll before the await and unconditionally restores it afterwards, so any legitimate change to the tail state during the clipboard promise (user scrolls up, or hits Pause/Resume — a real window when the browser shows a clipboard permission prompt and writeText stays pending) is silently clobbered back to the pre-click value. The save/restore is also unnecessary: nothing in the click path scrolls the stream (@mousedown.prevent suppresses focus), so onScroll never fires, making the guard a net negative.

The 'leaves a paused tail paused' spec is vacuous: nothing in copyEntry can alter autoScroll in the test environment (no scroll is generated by a click), so the assertion passes identically with the save/restore lines deleted. It claims to protect auto-scroll behaviour on copy but exercises no code path that could break it.

triageGrades.reason: The diff only adds a view-level copy button, CSS and a spec; no auth middleware, token, role or gating logic is touched.
No credentials, env vars or key handling appear in the change (the copied string is log text already rendered on screen).
No billing, Stripe, pricing, quota or usage code is involved.
Nothing is deleted or overwritten; the existing clearLogs path is untouched and the new handler only reads an entry.
navigator.clipboard is a browser API, not a third-party service call, and the change adds no new network requests or endpoints.
No build, deploy, nixpacks or runtime config is modified; the only non-view edit is adding Vuetify component stubs to the test harness.

summary: The local model found nothing, which is defensible here — the change is small and essentially correct — but it also offered no verification of the two things the item actually hinges on (the copied string and the auto-scroll guarantee), and missed the pointless-and-slightly-harmful autoScroll save/restore plus the vacuous spec that purports to cover it.
